newsitem.title: QATAR: Jordan backs four-way meeting on peace process.
newsitem.headline: Jordan backs four-way meeting on peace process.

text.p: Jordan's prime minister said on Monday his country would attend a mini-summit proposed by Egypt to help restart the stalled Middle East peace process.

"We welcome (Egyptian) President Hosni Mubarak's initiative to convene a summit of four leaders to bring the peace process back on track and we are eager to attend," Abdul-Salam al-Majali told reporters after official talks in Doha.
"We think a summit of this nature is important at this critical juncture," he added.

Mubarak has said he is willing to call a regional summit if Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shows a willingness to back down on a controversial Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Israeli-Palestinian talks have been suspended because of the construction.
Those taking part at the summit would be Mubarak, Netanyahu, King Hussein of Jordan and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Mubarak said last week.
Jordan and Egypt, who have peace treaties with Israel, often mediate in negotiations between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.

Majali arrived in Qatar on Saturday on a three-day official visit to help boost bilateral ties. He is accompanied by the Jordanian ministers of energy, labour and information on his first trip abroad since becoming prime minister last month.
Both countries discussed closer energy and industrial links and signed protocols to boost information cooperation and manpower training, officials said.
Jordanian-Qatari ties have improved dramatically since a chill caused by the 1990 Gulf crisis.
Jordan angered its Gulf Arab allies by backing Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Amman wants Gulf states to employ more Jordanians to help ease soaring unemployment.
